name: Toi
overview: Toi was a male king known as the King of Hamath, a title indicating his rule over the city of Hamath. The biblical record identifies him primarily by this royal position, with no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Toi appears as a proper name in Scripture, with an alternate form, Tou, also recorded. His title, King of Hamath, straightforwardly identifies his political authority over the city of Hamath. No further meaning is given for his names in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records a relationship between Toi and Joram, identifying Joram as Toi's father by inference. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Toi's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as a regional monarch during the time of King David's reign. His mention alongside interactions with Israelite kings highlights the political and military dynamics of the period. Toi's presence in Scripture underscores the wider geopolitical context in which God's people lived and served the Lord.
